skill.name: journey-map
skill.description: Create customer journey maps for user flows and workflows. Use when the user asks to "map the journey", "analyze user flow", "document the workflow", "trace the path", or needs to understand end-to-end user experiences.
skill.summary: Create structured customer journey maps for user flows, workflows, touchpoints, emotions, and improvement planning.
skill.author: Dami-Randle

content.value_statement: Teams need clear views of how users move through a service. This skill creates structured journey maps that expose actions, emotions, pain points, and opportunities.
actual_capabilities: Defines persona, goal, trigger, and success context for a journey.
Breaks journeys into phases, steps, touchpoints, and interfaces.
Documents user actions, thoughts, emotions, pain points, and opportunities.
Creates emotion curves and concise key insights.
Produces prioritized recommendations with expected impact.
limitations: It does not validate findings with users unless research data is provided.
It does not collect analytics data or observe real behavior.
It needs enough context about the persona, product, and task.
LogiDocs Certify examples may need adaptation for other products.

use_cases.title: Improve Onboarding
use_cases.description: Map a first-time user path and identify friction before design or engineering work begins.

use_cases.title: Analyze Research Findings
use_cases.description: Convert interviews, observations, or support notes into a structured journey map.

use_cases.title: Document Compliance Workflows
use_cases.description: Trace certificate uploads, audit preparation, or expiring document workflows across teams.

prompt_templates.title: Map a Basic Journey
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a customer journey map for [persona] who wants to [goal]. Include phases, steps, emotions, pain points, and opportunities.

prompt_templates.title: Analyze an Existing Flow
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze this workflow: [steps]. Identify friction, emotional changes, missing information, and improvement opportunities.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Persona Paths
prompt_templates.prompt: Create journey maps for [persona A] and [persona B] completing [task]. Compare triggers, concerns, touchpoints, and recommendations.

prompt_templates.title: Prioritize Journey Improvements
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this journey context: [details]. Produce a detailed map, emotion curve, key insights, and prioritized recommendations with impact.

output_examples.input: Map the first-time onboarding journey for a small business admin.
output_examples.output: A journey map with context, phase table, detailed steps, emotion curve, key insights, and prioritized onboarding recommendations.

output_examples.input: Analyze the supplier certificate upload workflow.
output_examples.output: A workflow journey that highlights upload touchpoints, confusion points, emotional dips, and high-impact improvements.

output_examples.input: Compare how two personas prepare for an audit.
output_examples.output: Two persona-specific journey maps with shared bottlenecks, unique concerns, and prioritized changes for audit readiness.

best_practices: Provide the persona, task, product context, and any known journey steps.
Include user research, support notes, or analytics summaries when available.
Ask for priority levels when recommendations will guide planning decisions.
anti_patterns: Do not treat the map as validated research without user evidence.
Do not ask for a full journey when only a single screen needs review.
Do not omit constraints such as compliance rules, roles, or handoffs.

faq.question: What does this skill create?
faq.answer: It creates customer journey maps for user flows, workflows, and end-to-end service experiences.

faq.question: Can it map an existing product flow?
faq.answer: Yes. Provide the current steps, screens, roles, and known issues for better results.

faq.question: Does it replace user research?
faq.answer: No. It organizes available context and highlights gaps that research should verify.

faq.question: Can it support product planning?
faq.answer: Yes. It can turn journey pain points into prioritized recommendations with expected impact.

faq.question: Is it only for LogiDocs Certify?
faq.answer: No. The examples mention LogiDocs Certify, but the mapping structure works for other products.

faq.question: What input improves the output?
faq.answer: The best input includes persona details, goals, triggers, current steps, pain points, and success criteria.
